[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Mark chops that outrun their lumberjack's interval in the AXE tab[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]The AXE tab visibly marks every chop whose run time reaches or [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]exceeds its lumberjack's interval — on the sidebar row, in the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]lumberjack overview table, and in the chop detail header — so the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]operator can tell at a glance which chop is stretching its [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]lumberjack's cycle and needs a longer interval or a lumberjack of [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]its own.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]4[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]3[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Overrun classifier in the Rust core[/bold #D7AFFF]                           [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]core_classifier[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]core_classifier: add the host-I/O-free `axe_overrun` module, its [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]versioned wire records, and the `classify_chop_overrun` PyO3 binding [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]that turns one chop's cached run history plus its lumberjack interval [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]into a level/ratio verdict.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Record how long a chop actually blocked its tick[/bold #D7AFFF]              [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]blocking_duration[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]blocking_duration: persist `script_duration_ms` on chop run entries so [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]an agent-launching run keeps its script wall-clock after lifecycle [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]finalization overwrites `duration_ms`, and make the run-entry reader [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]tolerate unknown keys.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Classify each chop while collecting AXE snapshots[/bold #D7AFFF]             [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]snapshot_wiring[dim] · [dim][/dim]after core_classifier, blocking_duration[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]snapshot_wiring: add the typed Python facade, carry the effective [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]interval and the verdict on `ChopSnapshot`/`LumberjackSnapshot`, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]compute both on the full collector and the targeted single-chop refresh [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]path.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Render the overrun mark across the AXE tab[/bold #D7AFFF]                    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]tab_indicator[dim] · [dim][/dim]after snapshot_wiring[/#AF87FF][/dim]

    [#D7D7AF]overview table's PACE column and advisory line, the chop detail header [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]segment, the help guide legend, docs, and the PNG snapshots that pin all[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]of it.[/#D7D7AF]
